rows.commute: Journeys to work by main mode
rows.education: Residents aged 25-64 by highest level of education
rows.nativity: Residents by country of birth (or citizenship)

notes.all: Urban Audit rows take the functional urban area's figures (geo …F, level "fua") when Eurostat publishes them, else the core city's (…C, level "city"), from the latest year in which every category of the row is published (year). A row Eurostat does not publish for the area is null, never zeros. Europe = the sum of the urban areas that have the row (years differ between cities).
notes.workforce: Jobs by branch of activity, counted where people work (Eurostat regional accounts, NUTS 3 employment by branch apportioned to the urban area by population: cities.json jobs). Eurostat publishes no occupation split for cities, so each category is a branch, drawn with the nearest occupation's figure.
notes.age: Residents on 1 January by age group (Urban Audit urb_lpop1 for functional urban areas, urb_cpop1 for core cities), latest year with every group. Median age: interpolated within the 5-year age groups (a 10-year group published only as a whole is split evenly), the same way for every city and for Europe; the statistical office's own median (DE1073V, urb_lpopstr / urb_cpopstr) is kept as median_published.
notes.commute: Journeys to work by main mode (Urban Audit urb_ltran / urb_ctran, shares in %), rescaled to the four modes published, times the area's employed residents (active − unemployed, EC1001V − EC1010V; else employed aged 20-64, EC1177V; else jobs, EC2020V; else cities.json employed). Carpooling and working from home are not published.
notes.education: Residents aged 25-64 by highest level of education completed, ISCED 2011 (Urban Audit urb_leduc / urb_ceduc).
notes.nativity: Residents by country of birth: this country, another EU country, outside the EU (Urban Audit urb_lpopcb / urb_cpopcb). Where country of birth is not published, by citizenship: nationals, other EU citizens, non-EU citizens (the row's basis says which).

workforce.label: Finance, insurance and real estate
workforce.lines: cities.json jobs: finance + real_estate (NACE K, L)

workforce.label: Information, professional, scientific, technical and support services
workforce.lines: cities.json jobs: information + professional (NACE J, M, N)

workforce.label: Public administration, education, health and social work
Industry: manufacturing, mining, energy, water and waste

age.label: 15 to 34
age.lines: DE1046V + DE1049V + DE1058V (15-19, 20-24, 25-34; 25-34 = DE1101V + DE1104V where only 5-year groups are published)

age.label: 35 to 64
age.lines: DE1061V + DE1064V + DE1025V (35-44, 45-54, 55-64; or their 5-year groups DE1107V + DE1110V, DE1113V + DE1116V, DE1119V + DE1122V)

commute.label: Car
commute.lines: TT1003V (share of journeys to work by car)

commute.label: Bicycle or motorcycle
commute.lines: TT1007V + TT1006V (motorcycle = TT1012V − TT1003V where TT1006V is not published)

education.label: Tertiary: short-cycle, bachelor's, master's or doctorate (ISCED 5-8)

nativity.label: Born in another EU country
nativity.lines: DE2010V foreign-born in an EU country (citizenship basis: DE2002V EU foreigners)

nativity.label: Born outside the EU
nativity.lines: DE2011V foreign-born in a non-EU country, or DE2009V − DE2010V (citizenship basis: DE2003V non-EU foreigners, or DE2012V − DE2002V)

rule.text: A category is a specialty when its share is at least 1.5× the European share (up to 4, strongest first) or at most 0.67× (up to 2); categories under 1% both here and across Europe are skipped. Europe = the sum of the urban areas that have the row (citizenship-basis origins are compared with Europe by citizenship).
